what_it_does: Self-driving car software continuously runs many perception modules — camera processing, object detection, lane tracking — regardless of whether those modules are actually relevant to the current driving situation, burning compute power on scenes that need no special attention. AnA redesigns the interface between the perception system (which senses the world) and the planning system (which decides what to do) so that the planner can tell the perception system exactly what to watch for. The perception system then runs only the tasks that matter for the current context, switches between a broad low-cost awareness mode and a targeted high-fidelity mode on safety-critical objects, and monitors for unexpected situations. This mirrors how a human driver shifts focused attention rather than processing everything equally at all times.
